headline: Raises VA disability and survivor payments by the same percentage as the Social Security cost-of-living increase starting December 1, 2026.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to raise several benefit amounts by the same percentage as the Social Security cost-of-living increase that takes effect December 1, 2026. This covers disability compensation, extra payments for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and payments to surviving spouses and children. The VA must publish the new amounts in the Federal Register. The VA may also make a similar increase for certain other people receiving disability compensation.

who_it_affects.how: Their monthly disability compensation goes up by the same percentage as the Social Security cost-of-living increase.

who_it_affects.group: Disabled veterans with spouses, children, or dependent parents
who_it_affects.how: The extra amounts they receive for dependents also go up by the same percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Disabled veterans who get a clothing allowance
who_it_affects.how: Their yearly clothing allowance, paid to certain veterans whose disability or equipment damages clothing, is increased.

who_it_affects.group: Surviving spouses and children of veterans
who_it_affects.how: Their dependency and indemnity compensation payments go up by the same percentage.
